---
title: "Policies"
---

The syllabus in Canvas is the official version of every course policy. This page
summarizes the ones you'll use most.

## AI use

AI assistants are allowed in this course, with acknowledgment, under rules that
change as your skills grow. You must be able to explain and defend every line you
submit.

| Period | Chat assistants (explain, debug) | Inline autocomplete | Agentic tools that edit and run code for you | Disclosure |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Weeks 1–5 (fundamentals, data) | Allowed | **Off** | Not for problem sets | AI usage note on every problem set |
| Weeks 6–13 (numerical methods, applications) | Allowed | Allowed | Not for problem sets | AI usage note on every problem set |
| Weeks 14–16 and capstone | Allowed | Allowed | Allowed, documented | Usage note, plus one AI error your team caught and corrected, in the presentation |
| Midterm and in-class exams | Not allowed | Off | Not allowed | — |

**Why autocomplete is off at first:** in the first five weeks, autocomplete writes
the syntax you're supposed to be learning. A chat assistant explaining an error
message teaches it.

**Tools:** Microsoft 365 Copilot Chat is free with your WSU login and is the
course default. GitHub Copilot is free for verified students through GitHub
Education. You may use other assistants under the same rules; you never need to
pay for one. In course codespaces, Copilot's autocomplete is switched off for Weeks 1–5;
you'll be shown how to turn it on in Week 6. Copilot Chat stays available.

**Privacy:** never paste personal data, other students' work, or restricted
datasets into a consumer AI tool. Use the WSU-login Copilot when unsure.

**Spot checks:** each week a few students, chosen at random, walk through one
cell of their submission for three minutes in lab or office hours.

### AI usage note

Every problem-set notebook ends with this cell. "None" is a fine answer.

```markdown
## AI usage note
- Tool(s) and model, if known:
- What I asked (paste or summarize the key prompts):
- What I used from the output, and where (cell numbers):
- How I checked it (tests run, numbers compared, errors I fixed):
```

## Submitting work

1. Restart & Run All. The notebook must run from top to bottom.
2. Fill in the AI usage note.
3. Commit and push.
4. Copy the commit URL from GitHub and paste it into the Canvas assignment before
   the deadline. **The Canvas submission time is the official time.**
